description: Constraints are deliberately absent: Renovate reads them from package.json engines (node >=22.17), which is the floor the code has to run on. A literal here was a second source of truth that nothing verified — it said node 24 while engines said 22, so Renovate was free to pick a dependency the declared floor cannot run.

The Node version CI and the deploys run lives in .nvmrc, read by every workflow through .github/actions/node-setup. Renovate's nvm manager updates that file; a `node-version:` literal in a workflow is invisible to every manager it has.

Lock file maintenance runs at any time: the preset's default window (Monday before 04:00) was narrower than Renovate's own visits, so the lock file went untouched from 13 September while a fixed brace-expansion sat on npm; nothing else refreshes a transitive dependency.

packageRules.description: Two versions of github-pages-deploy-action write gh-pages: the one deploy.yml pins, and the one rossjrw/pr-preview-action pins inside itself, which no manager can see. Keeping the two actions in one PR is the nearest thing to a reminder: when either bumps, check the nested pin in the preview action's action.yml against deploy.yml's.
Types track the engines floor (Node >=22.17), not CI's Node 24 runtime — keeps Node-23+/24-only APIs out of code that must still run on 22.
TS 7 (native compiler) is out of peer range for typescript-eslint (>=4.8.4 <6.1.0, crashes at runtime) and @sveltejs/kit (^5.3.3 || ^6.0.0). Drop this rule once both support it.
requires-python names the minor only: push/.python-version already picks the interpreter.
push/.python-version picks the interpreter for CI and the image alike, and requires-python must name the same minor: one PR for both. Held at 3.14 with the homelab repositories.
